source.behavior: DateOnly overload converts to a Cairo single-day range. Range overload calls shared LoadSalesOrdersAsync (AsNoTracking orders + items, current cancelled status excluded, optional UTC half-open business-date and nonempty shift filters), maps snapshots to domain Orders, finds cash-on-delivery IDs lacking any settled custody, then delegates all calculation to SalesRules.ComputeSalesReport and maps its output to SalesReportDto. Query is read-only.

cross_file_evidence.behavior: Computes gross as frozen order Total, refunds as RefundAmount, net = gross-refunds; splits offer/comps/manual discount values; pending electronic sum is removed from collected; COD orders without settled custody are removed from collected and reported as CashWithDrivers; channel totals come from OrderPaymentQueries; average is integer-piastres net divided by order count; order-type totals net refunds. No writes or live price/tax recalculation.

COD eligibility reuses CheckoutRules.IsCashOnDelivery and excludes IDs with a settled custody; comment identifies settlement movement into main treasury as point restaurant holds cash. Shortages are reported separately to avoid subtracting them twice.

Payment channel totals include a single-method order only when IsPaid; multi-method cash/card legs count immediately, electronic legs only after confirmation. Doc spells out split/refund behavior. COD remains excluded from drawer payment-channel totals because Order.IsPaid is frozen false for COD; overall CollectedSales separately admits COD after driver settlement. This is consistent with settlement being posted to treasury main rather than drawer, though tests principally assert cash basis fields rather than channel cash after settlement.
Sales route resolves from/to/businessDate and requires reports_view before returning the report.
DTO reports gross/refund/net, payment channels, uncollected COD, pending electronic amounts, and order-type/discount values separately.
Covers basic cash sale and takeaway, discount/comps/offer buckets, reports_view denial, cross-report empty shiftId regression and explicit shift filtering. No test ran.

End-to-end source tests trace cash-on-delivery through New/Ready/Assigned/Delivered/Settled and assert CashWithDrivers/CollectedSales; prepaid pending electronic path stays uncollected. Does not assert cash channel's COD treatment after settlement.
Daily statement flow test confirms unsettled COD and pending electronic visibility; source asserts the same report composition via daily statement.

assessment.financial_relevance: High; exposes revenue, refunds and collection status. Distinguishes sale recognition from cash held and channel allocation.
observations: Orders are based on frozen checkout facts; new live pricing/tax configuration does not rewrite historical figures.
CollectedSales is a cash-basis figure: net sales less unconfirmed electronic claims and unsettled COD; delivery lifecycle tests cover transitions, including settled custody becoming collected.

Cash/PaymentMethod totals are drawer/payment-channel figures and not interchangeable with CollectedSales (COD settlement enters main treasury, while COD Order.IsPaid remains false). This interpretive distinction should be explicit in UI but source distinguishes CashWithDrivers and CollectedSales; no mismatch proven.

Average order value divides net sales by count of eligible noncancelled orders including pending electronic orders; this is order-value average, not collected-cash average. No source contract says otherwise.
counterevidence: SalesRules comments and tests explicitly establish exclusion of pending electronic sales and unsettled COD from collected sales; a naive interpretation that gross/net must equal cash would be wrong.
PaymentMethodTotals documentation describes channel amounts and gate on confirmation/IsPaid; COD is intentionally not a drawer receipt before/after driver remits to main treasury.
Shared SQL status predicate collation behavior is runtime/provider dependent and was already outside this batch; no such conclusion is asserted.
